subject: basic-computing
title: Customer Services
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: What should be your first step to make a customer happy?
questions.answer: Greet the customer with a smile and a welcome message.

questions.q: Why should short forms of words or sentences not be used while communicating with a customer?
questions.answer: Jargon and acronyms such as ASAP or FYI may not be understood by the customer, so clear words should be used.

questions.q: State true or false: You can use jargons while interacting with a customer.
questions.answer: False.

questions.q: State true or false: Always greet your customer with a smile.
questions.answer: True.

questions.q: Who is the 'face of the business'?
questions.answer: The customer service representative.

questions.q: Why should you be formal even if the customer is friendly?
questions.answer: To keep a uniform, professional interaction; over-friendly behaviour may land you in trouble.

questions.q: How should you dress while dealing with customers?
questions.answer: Formally, neat and well groomed.

questions.q: What is an active listener?
questions.answer: One who focuses on what the customer says, uses positive body language and acknowledges before replying.

questions.q: What should you do if you cannot hear the customer clearly on the phone?
questions.answer: Politely say 'Kindly excuse, I am unable to hear you clearly' instead of asking them to speak clearly.

questions.q: Why should you never interrupt a customer?
questions.answer: Interruption is taken as an offence and may upset the customer.

questions.q: Name one way of seeking support while serving a customer.
questions.answer: Take help of colleagues or team members.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the main points to deliver excellent customer service.
questions.answer: Greet with a smile and offer help; give undivided attention; be courteous and formal; listen actively and never interrupt; use clear words; resolve and follow up until the issue is solved; know the product and company policy.

questions.q: (i) What is the importance of seeking support while dealing with customers? (ii) Why should you be formal while communicating with your customers?
questions.answer: (i) Colleagues may know a solution and each has a unique way of handling queries, so support helps resolve the issue. (ii) Formal language keeps interaction professional and avoids misunderstanding or trouble.

questions.q: (i) Why is giving undivided attention necessary for customer satisfaction? (ii) Why is it necessary to be dressed professionally?
questions.answer: (i) The customer feels valued and the query is solved quickly. (ii) A neat, decent appearance lets customers interact confidently and freely.

questions.q: What qualities are expected from a customer service representative?
questions.answer: Politeness, active listening, clear communication, knowledge of product and policies, patience and calm behaviour, ability to resolve problems.

questions.q: Why is it important to dress well as a customer representative?
questions.answer: A decent and groomed appearance creates a good first impression and gives customers confidence.

questions.q: Why should you not be over-friendly with the customer?
questions.answer: It may land you in trouble and affect uniformity and professionalism in interaction.

questions.q: List the basic communication skills required while interacting with the customer.
questions.answer: Active listening, not interrupting, clear words, courtesy, formal tone, positive statements, noting the preferred mode of communication.

questions.q: Why is it important to know the company policies as a customer service representative?
questions.answer: To resolve conflicts and answer queries correctly using latest, accurate information.

questions.q: Write a polite way to ask for a product's serial id.
questions.answer: 'Sir/Madam, can I have the serial id of the product?'

questions.q: Why should the representative follow up with the customer?
questions.answer: To ensure the complete resolution of the problem, which gives a satisfied customer and good word of mouth.

questions.q: What is meant by 'Pay undivided attention'?
questions.answer: Stopping all other work and attending to the customer's query first or guiding them politely to the right person.

questions.q: Why should you take notes and repeat what you understood?
questions.answer: To confirm the customer's requirement and seek approval, showing that you listened.

sections.title: Answer the questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain how to greet a customer.
questions.answer: Greet with a smile and welcome message, offer help without pressing what to buy, give undivided attention, remain formal and dress professionally.

questions.q: Explain any three basic communication points with a customer.
questions.answer: Be an active listener with eye contact and notes; use clear words without jargon; be courteous and positive, e.g. 'Sir/Madam, can I have the serial id?' instead of commanding.

questions.q: Assume you are at an IT helpdesk and a customer is annoyed since the engineer has not called. How will you resolve it?
questions.answer: Greet and apologise politely, verify the complaint number and details, listen without interrupting, assure follow-up, contact the engineer or department, give a time, and follow up until solved.

questions.q: Explain the key to excellent customer service.
questions.answer: Courteous handling and immediate response retain customers; follow up until resolution; know the product and policies; speak slowly and calmly; keep questions short.

questions.q: Explain how to handle situations of noise, preferred mode of communication and seeking support.
questions.answer: Move to a quiet place when on the phone; ask for the customer's preferred mode (e-mail or message); seek help from colleagues when stuck and learn from them.

questions.q: Why are words and phrases important when talking to customers? Give examples.
questions.answer: Right words keep the customer positive: say 'Kindly excuse, I am unable to hear you clearly' rather than 'Speak clearly'; use 'Is the computer starting?' instead of 'booting'.
